headline: Anthropic: CLAUDE.md vs Scripts vs Hooks
summary: Anthropic clarifies when to use CLAUDE.md instructions versus scripts or hooks in Claude Code. Each mechanism serves a distinct purpose: persistent context, one-off automation, and event-driven enforcement. Choosing correctly prevents context bloat and keeps team workflows clean.

slides.title: Your CLAUDE.md Is a Junk Drawer
slides.subtitle: Not every rule belongs in persistent context
slides.body: Teams stuff everything into CLAUDE.md — style guides, build commands, deployment steps. The file grows until the model drowns in irrelevant context. When does a rule belong elsewhere?
slides.deep_dive: CLAUDE.md loads into every conversation as system context. It's perfect for project-wide conventions: coding standards, architecture patterns, testing philosophy. But it becomes a liability when filled with situational commands, one-time setup steps, or rules that only apply during specific workflows. The model pays attention cost for every token, and irrelevant context degrades reasoning on the actual task.
slides.key_fact: CLAUDE.md loads as persistent context in every Claude Code session
slides.why_it_matters: Bloated context windows reduce model accuracy on your actual coding task

slides.title: Three Mechanisms, Three Jobs
slides.subtitle: CLAUDE.md, scripts, and hooks each solve different problems
slides.body: CLAUDE.md = persistent project knowledge. Scripts = reusable automation. Hooks = event-triggered enforcement. Pick the right tool for the rule's lifecycle.
slides.deep_dive: Think of it like a kitchen: CLAUDE.md is the recipe book everyone references (persistent knowledge). Scripts are appliances — blender, food processor — you pull out for specific prep tasks (on-demand automation). Hooks are the smoke detector and timer — they react automatically when something happens (event-driven guardrails). Each has a distinct trigger model and persistence profile.
slides.key_fact: Three distinct automation primitives with different trigger models
slides.why_it_matters: Matching mechanism to use case prevents context pollution and missed enforcement

slides.title: How Each Mechanism Activates
slides.subtitle: Different triggers, different persistence
slides.body: CLAUDE.md loads automatically. Scripts run on demand. Hooks fire on events. The activation model determines what fits where.
slides.deep_dive: CLAUDE.md is injected into the system prompt at session start — always present. Scripts are invoked explicitly by you or the agent via tool calls — ephemeral, purpose-built. Hooks register with the runtime (pre-tool-use, post-tool-use, notification) and execute automatically when their event fires — invisible guardrails. This fundamental difference in 'when they run' dictates 'what they should contain.'
slides.key_fact: Activation model (automatic vs on-demand vs event-driven) determines proper use case
slides.why_it_matters: Rules that shouldn't persist in context belong in scripts or hooks

slides.title: Where Each Lives in the Stack
slides.subtitle: Editor → Agent → Context → Execution
slides.body: CLAUDE.md sits in context layer. Scripts live in tool layer. Hooks hook into runtime events. Clean separation prevents leakage.
slides.deep_dive: Visualize the request flow: Your editor sends input to the local agent. The agent assembles context — CLAUDE.md is baked in here. When the agent needs to act, it calls tools — scripts are invokable tools here. Meanwhile, the runtime emits events (file write, command run) — hooks intercept these. Three distinct insertion points in the pipeline, each with different visibility and timing.
slides.key_fact: Three insertion points: context assembly, tool invocation, runtime events
slides.why_it_matters: Architecture placement determines scope, timing, and visibility of each rule

slides.title: From Trigger to Outcome
slides.subtitle: Each mechanism transforms input differently
slides.body: CLAUDE.md shapes reasoning. Scripts produce artifacts. Hooks gate or mutate operations. The output type reveals the right choice.
slides.deep_dive: When you ask 'refactor this module,' CLAUDE.md influences how the agent thinks (style, patterns). When you run a script 'generate-api-docs,' it produces a file artifact. When a hook fires on 'pre-write,' it can block, modify, or log the operation. CLAUDE.md = cognitive influence. Scripts = artifact generation. Hooks = operational guardrails. The desired output — changed thinking, created file, or controlled action — maps directly to the mechanism.
slides.key_fact: Output type (influence, artifact, gate) determines mechanism selection
slides.why_it_matters: Don't use a hook to generate docs. Don't use CLAUDE.md to run builds.
slides.processing: Context injection (CLAUDE.md) → Tool invocation (scripts) → Event interception (hooks)
slides.output: Shaped reasoning | Generated artifacts | Gated operations

slides.title: Antipatterns That Bloat Context
slides.subtitle: Stop putting these in CLAUDE.md
slides.body: Build commands, one-time setup, personal preferences, deprecated rules — these belong in scripts, docs, or hooks. Not in every conversation.
slides.deep_dive: Common mistakes: storing 'npm run build' in CLAUDE.md (use a script), adding 'run tests before commit' (use a pre-commit hook), keeping old migration steps (archive to docs), personal editor config (local settings only). Each adds tokens to every prompt without proportional value. The fix: audit CLAUDE.md quarterly. If a rule hasn't been relevant in 10 sessions, move it. Scripts for commands. Hooks for enforcement. Docs for reference.
slides.key_fact: Irrelevant CLAUDE.md entries degrade model performance on every task
slides.why_it_matters: Context hygiene directly impacts coding agent accuracy

slides.title: Audit Your CLAUDE.md This Week
slides.subtitle: Move situational rules to scripts and hooks
slides.body: Three-step cleanup: list every CLAUDE.md entry, classify by trigger type, migrate to the right mechanism. Your context window will thank you.
slides.deep_dive: Start by opening CLAUDE.md and tagging each section: [PERSISTENT] for always-relevant conventions, [COMMAND] for runnable steps, [GUARDRAIL] for enforcement rules. Create a .claude/scripts/ folder for commands. Configure hooks in .claude/settings.json for guardrails. Move reference material to docs/. The result: a lean CLAUDE.md that actually shapes reasoning, plus discoverable scripts and invisible hooks that fire exactly when needed.
slides.key_fact: Lean CLAUDE.md + targeted scripts + event hooks = cleaner context, reliable automation
slides.why_it_matters: Proper mechanism assignment scales team workflows without context bloat
takeaways: Audit CLAUDE.md: tag each rule by trigger type
Configure enforcement via hooks in settings.json
